correctness.rationale: The primary source explicitly reduces Newton(F) to the convex hull of at most m+1 Schur permutahedra determined by alpha and beta. Minimum-enclosing-center uniqueness plus coordinate-permutation symmetry forces a diagonal center. At a diagonal center c, the squared distance of layer i differs from layer i-1 by \(2( eta_i-lpha_i)(h_i-c)\); monotonicity of the partition midpoints therefore makes the maximum layer radius equal the coordinatewise far-endpoint sum Phi(c). Phi is strongly convex. On each midpoint interval it is one explicit quadratic with mean c_i, yielding the stated finite scan. Strict convexity of the ball proves that the listed active source orbit points are exactly the contacts.

value.rationale: Good symmetric polynomials are a broad source family introduced to unify Newton-polytope saturation and IDP results for many symmetric-polynomial classes. Their Newton polytopes can have very large monomial supports and multiple total-degree layers. The theorem gives a complete exact minimum-sphere solution for every member from only the two endpoint partitions, reducing the problem to an O(m) scalar scan and explicitly identifying the contact layers. The inflated Grothendieck example shows a genuinely multilayer phenomenon: the top-degree endpoint is not a contact, while two lower layers jointly control the sphere.
